correctness.rationale: The function-space coefficient matrix decomposition gives exactly two unconditional pivots and a separate pivot for each nonzero interpolation coefficient. The coefficient identity h_r=(alpha^(p-1-r)+beta^(p-1-r))/(alpha-beta)^2 follows from partial fractions and finite geometric sums over F_p*, so its zeros are exactly z^(p-1-r)=-1. Counting these k except k=2 proves each rank case, including t=2,4 boundary exceptions; Smith normal form proves p^(1+delta) determinant divisibility, with no claim of sharp valuation. A standalone test computes 724 independent ranks and root-ratio orders for all anisotropic pairs at p=5,7,11,13,17,19,23; finite checks do not replace universal proof.

value.rationale: The invariant is the exact rank of the same full arithmetic matrix used to prove Sun's p^2 congruence. It gives an order-theoretic stratification of exceptional congruence strength, e.g. p=19,(c,d)=(1,10) gives rank 15 and p^4 divisibility versus generic p^2. The uniform all-prime formula both accounts for a previously isolated coefficient cancellation and distinguishes structurally meaningful torsion strata; it is neither an arbitrary finite slice nor a mere numerical recomputation.
